card: Fixes an intermittent CI race in feature_torcontrol.py by tracking the connection acceptance timestamp on the mock Tor server instead of relying on the test thread's polling loop timing. The test previously failed (observed on NetBSD and tracked in #36934) when the node reconnected before the test began checking backoff delays. Resolving this removes flaky test failures in CI without relaxing the backoff or protocol verification requirements.
evidence: Fixes linked issue #36934 ('qa: Intermittent failure in feature_torcontrol.py').
Description notes: 'This caused an intermittent CI failure on NetBSD even though the node observed the expected delay.'
Description notes: 'On Linux, the 1.5-second delay from the issue reproduced the original failure. The updated test passed both with and without that delay.'
problem: The Tor control functional test fails intermittently in CI (observed on NetBSD) because thread scheduling can allow the node to complete its reconnect backoff and establish a connection before the test checks for it, causing false-positive test failures.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause test suite failures or fail to catch regressions in Tor control reconnect backoff logic.

scope_notes: Small test-only change (+8/-4 in one file), but the diff was omitted from the prompt.
summary: Fixes a timing race in feature_torcontrol.py where the test could fail if bitcoind reconnects to the mock Tor control service before the test runner thread begins polling for the reconnect backoff. The test now records the timestamp when the mock Tor server accepts the incoming connection and checks the elapsed time against the pre-disconnect timestamp.
